Slide.Title: tall (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: tall (adjective) Definition: Definition: higher than others; opposite of “short” Synonyms: Synonyms: high Examples: Examples: I am five feet, two inches tall. Most basketball players are very tall. The bridge is very long, and very tall. The bridge is very long and very tall.

Slide.Title: target (noun)
Slide.SlideText: target (noun) Definition: Definition: an object or person that is aimed or fired at, usually with a gun Synonyms: Synonyms: bull’s eye, mark Examples: Examples: Her shot missed the target by two feet. The center of a target is called a “bull’s eye.” Archery is a sport of shooting arrows at a target. You hit the center of the target. You hit the center of the target.

Slide.Title: taste (verb)
Slide.SlideText: taste (verb) Definition: Definition: to sense through the mouth Synonyms: Synonyms: savor Examples: Examples: The fruit tastes sweet. When I have a cold, I cannot taste anything. Watermelon tastes delicious on a hot day. Watermelon tastes delicious on a hot day.

Slide.Title: tax (noun)
Slide.SlideText: tax (noun) Definition: Definition: the money a person or business must pay to the government so the government can provide services Synonyms: Synonyms: duty, tariff Examples: Examples: He pays about 25% of his income in taxes. Many people hire accountants to help them with their tax returns. All Americans have to pay their taxes. All Americans have to pay their taxes.

Slide.Title: team (noun)
Slide.SlideText: team (noun) Definition: Definition: a group organized for some purpose, often for sports Synonyms: Synonyms: club, squad Examples: Examples: The water polo team practices at 5:30 a.m. He is the captain of the football team. My son practices with his Little League baseball team every weekend. My son practices with his Little League baseball team every weekend.

Slide.Title: tear (verb)
Slide.SlideText: tear (verb) Definition: Definition: to pull apart, often by force Synonyms: Synonyms: rip, cut Examples: Examples: I tear my clothes when I work in the garden. She tore the paper in half. I tore a hole in my jeans when I fell off my bike. I tore a hole in my jeans when I fell off my bike..

Slide.Title: technical (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: technical (adjective) Definition: Definition: involving machines, processes, and materials; of or about a very special kind of subject or thing Synonyms: Synonyms: high-tech, specialized Examples: Examples: You need technical knowledge to understand how this system works. The programmer is fixing a technical problem with the computer server. The programmer is fixing a technical problem with the computer server.

Slide.Title: telescope (noun)
Slide.SlideText: telescope (noun) Definition: Definition: a device for making objects that are far away appear closer and larger Synonyms: Synonyms: Examples: Examples: The world’s largest telescope is in the Canary Islands. They are using a telescope to look at the sky. You can see the stars using a telescope. You can see the stars using a telescope.

Slide.Title: temperature (noun)
Slide.SlideText: temperature (noun) Definition: Definition: the measurement of heat and cold Synonyms: Synonyms: climate, thermal reading Examples: Examples: What is the temperature of the water in the pool? A thermostat tells the temperature of a room. The thermometer showed a temperature of 1020F. The thermometer showed a temperature of 102 0F.

Slide.Title: temporary (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: temporary (adjective) Definition: Definition: lasting only a short time Synonyms: Synonyms: fleeting, transient Examples: Examples: The company hired a temporary office assistant. The dentist put in a temporary filling. The roadblock is only temporary. It will be removed when the construction is finished. The roadblock is only temporary. It will be removed when the construction is finished.

Slide.Title: tense (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: tense (adjective) Definition: Definition: stressed or fearful; opposite of “calm” Synonyms: Synonyms: anxious, worried Examples: Examples: Her meeting with her boss was very tense. I am always tense before I get on an airplane. Her job makes this businesswoman feel very tense. Her job makes this businesswoman feel very tense.

Slide.Title: term (noun)
Slide.SlideText: term (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) limited period of time to carry out a responsibility; 2) the conditions accepted by those involved in it Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) time; 2) stipulation, condition Examples: Examples: He served two terms in Congress. (time) By signing a contract, you agree to certain terms. (condition) By signing a contract, you agree to certain terms and conditions.

Slide.Title: terrible (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: terrible (adjective) Definition: Definition: very bad; causing terror or fear Synonyms: Synonyms: awful, horrible, vile Examples: Examples: We saw a terrible movie last night. There was a terrible accident on the freeway. Smoking is terrible for your health. Smoking is terrible for your health.

Slide.Title: territory (noun)
Slide.SlideText: territory (noun) Definition: Definition: a large area of land Synonyms: Synonyms: district, region Examples: Examples: We drove through unfamiliar territory. Some Canadian territories have almost no people. Russia has many regions, or territories. Russia has many regions, or territories.

Slide.Title: terror (noun)
Slide.SlideText: terror (noun) Definition: Definition: extreme fear; that which causes great fear Synonyms: Synonyms: fright, horror Examples: Examples: She could never forget the terror of war. Some people have a terror of mice. The vampire movie filled them with terror. The vampire movie filled them with terror.

Slide.Title: terrorist (noun)
Slide.SlideText: terrorist (noun) Definition: Definition: a person who carries out acts of extreme violence as a protest or a way to influence a government Synonyms: Synonyms: radical Examples: Examples: Terrorists blew up a bus. Terrorists attacked the World Trade Center in New York City in 2001. Terrorists attacked the World Trade Center in New York City in 2001.

Slide.Title: theater (noun)
Slide.SlideText: theater (noun) Definition: Definition: a place where movies are shown or plays are performed Synonyms: Synonyms: auditorium, cinema, hall, playhouse Examples: Examples: The theater in my neighborhood is being rebuilt. Would you like to go to the theater this evening? We waited in the movie theater for the film to start. We waited in the movie theater for the film to start.

Slide.Title: theory (noun)
Slide.SlideText: theory (noun) Definition: Definition: a possible explanation of why something exists or how something happens, but which is not yet proven Synonyms: Synonyms: belief, hypothesis Examples: Examples: Scientists are debating his theory about the disappearance of the dinosaurs. Albert Einstein’s theory of relativity is the most famous formula in the world. Albert Einstein’s theory of relativity is the most famous math formula in the world.

Slide.Title: these (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: these (adjective) Definition: Definition: of or about the people, places, or things nearby that have been spoken about already Synonyms: Synonyms: Examples: Examples: These keys are not mine. I got these earrings from my grandmother. These apples look very fresh. These apples look very fresh.

Slide.Title: thick (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: thick (adjective) Definition: Definition: 1) having a large distance between two opposite surfaces; 2) liquid consistency not to flow freely Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) broad, solid; 2) dense; 3) viscous Examples: Examples: The wall is two meters thick. (broad) The forest is very thick. (dense) I love thick, creamy mushroom soup. (viscous) This book is very thick. This book is very thick.

Slide.Title: thin (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: thin (adjective) Definition: Definition: having a small distance between two opposite surfaces; not fat; not wide; opposite of “thick” Synonyms: Synonyms: narrow, skinny, slim Examples: Examples: The dress is made of a thin fabric. The dough used for pancakes is thin. I think fashion models today are too thin. This laptop computer is very thin. This laptop computer is very thin.

Slide.Title: through (preposition)
Slide.SlideText: through (preposition) Definition: Definition: in at one end and out at the other Synonyms: Synonyms: via Examples: Examples: The ball flew through the air. We walked through thick bushes. Many trains pass through the old stone tunnel. Many trains pass through the old stone tunnel.

Slide.Title: throw (verb)
Slide.SlideText: throw (verb) Definition: Definition: to cause to go through the air by a movement of the arm Synonyms: Synonyms: propel, toss Examples: Examples: The boys are throwing a ball in the back yard. In baseball, the pitcher is the player who throws the ball. In baseball, the pitcher is the player who throws the ball.

Slide.Title: tie (verb)
Slide.SlideText: tie (verb) Definition: Definition: to join or hold together with some material such as string Synonyms: Synonyms: bond, connect, interlace Examples: Examples: The mother tied a ribbon in her daughter’s hair. She wrapped the package and tied it with strings. I always tie my shoes tightly before I go jogging. I always tie my shoes tightly before I go jogging.

Slide.Title: tie (noun)
Slide.SlideText: tie (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) anything that joins or unites; 2) links or connections Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) string, lace; 2) bond, alliance Examples: Examples: The two families have very close ties. (bond) The United States has close ties to Mexico. (alliance) The strings are tied together. The strings are tied together.

Slide.Title: tissue (noun)
Slide.SlideText: tissue (noun) Definition: Definition: living material; a group of cells that are similar in appearance and do the same thing Synonyms: Synonyms: flesh Examples: Examples: The patient’s lung tissue was damaged from years of working in a coal mine. Human skin tissue is divided into three layers: dead cells, epidermis, and dermis. Human skin tissue is divided into three layers: dead cells, epidermis, and dermis.

Slide.Title: tool (noun)
Slide.SlideText: tool (noun) Definition: Definition: any instrument or device designed to help one do work Synonyms: Synonyms: device, gadget, instrument Examples: Examples: I need a tool for pulling weeds in my garden. What is the most important tool ever invented? The plumber used many tools to fix our sink. A wrench is a commonly used tool. A wrench is a commonly used tool.

Slide.Title: top (noun)
Slide.SlideText: top (noun) Definition: Definition: the upper edge or surface; the highest part Synonyms: Synonyms: roof; apex, peak Examples: Examples: She filled the bucket to the top. He put his wallet on top of the dresser. Do you think she will reach the top of the mountain? Do you think she will reach the top of the mountain?

Slide.Title: torture (verb)
Slide.SlideText: torture (verb) Definition: Definition: to cause severe pain; to use physical or mental punishment Synonyms: Synonyms: abuse, torment Examples: Examples: In the U.S., it is illegal to torture people in order to get information from them. The boss tortured the workers with his criticism. Her back pain was torturing her. Her back pain was torturing her.

Slide.Title: torture (noun)
Slide.SlideText: torture (noun) Definition: Definition: the act of causing severe pain in order to harm, punish, or get information Synonyms: Synonyms: agony, anguish, torment Examples: Examples: It was torture for him to see his girlfriend with another man. The terrorist used torture to force the man to give them information. It is illegal, in the United States, for law enforcement to use torture to get information.

Slide.Title: touch (verb)
Slide.SlideText: touch (verb) Definition: Definition: to put the hand or fingers on something or someone Synonyms: Synonyms: feel, grope Examples: Examples: Please do not touch the merchandise. Have you ever touched a dolphin? Blind people read by touching, using a system of raised dots called Braille. Blind people read by touching using a system of raised dots called Braille.

Slide.Title: toward(s) (preposition)
Slide.SlideText: toward(s) (preposition) Definition: Definition: in the direction of; leading to Synonyms: Synonyms: to Examples: Examples: It finally stopped raining towards evening. They walked toward the gate. The confused travelers realized they were going toward the wrong town. The confused travelers realized they were headed toward the wrong town.

Slide.Title: town (noun)
Slide.SlideText: town (noun) Definition: Definition: a center where people live, larger than a village but not as large as a city Synonyms: Synonyms: municipality Examples: Examples: The town was established in the 18th century. Life in a small town is boring. My hometown is located about 20 minutes from a large city. My hometown is located about 20 minutes from a large city.

Slide.Title: trade (noun)
Slide.SlideText: trade (noun) Definition: Definition: the activity of buying, selling, or exchanging products or services Synonyms: Synonyms: commerce, deal, transaction Examples: Examples: The two stamp collectors arranged a trade. Trade between two countries can be complex. There has been a large increase in trade between the United States and China. There has been a large increase in trade between the United States and China

Slide.Title: tragic (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: tragic (adjective) Definition: Definition: extremely sad; terrible Synonyms: Synonyms: awful, dreadful, sorrowful Examples: Examples: The tragic mistake affected many people. They both cried after hearing the tragic news. After hearing the tragic news, he went outside to be alone. After hearing the tragic news, he went outside to be alone.

Slide.Title: train (verb)
Slide.SlideText: train (verb) Definition: Definition: to teach or learn how to do something; to prepare for an activity Synonyms: Synonyms: coach, discipline, teach Examples: Examples: He was trained as a doctor. I trained my dog to bring me the newspaper in the morning. To teach the class is to train the class. To teach the class is to train the class.

Slide.Title: transport (verb)
Slide.SlideText: transport (verb) Definition: Definition: to move goods or people from one place to another Synonyms: Synonyms: move, transfer Examples: Examples: They hired a moving company to transport their belongings to their new home. Many goods are transported across the globe by ship. Many goods are transported across the globe by ship.

Slide.Title: trap (noun)
Slide.SlideText: trap (noun) Definition: Definition: a device used to catch animals Synonyms: Synonyms: snare Examples: Examples: Steel traps are illegal. We set out traps for catching cockroaches. The mouse was lured into the trap by a big piece of cheese. The mouse was lured into the trap by a big piece of cheese.

Slide.Title: treason (noun)
Slide.SlideText: treason (noun) Definition: Definition: the act of fighting against one’s own country or of helping its enemies Synonyms: Synonyms: disloyalty, treachery Examples: Examples: It is an act of treason to sell military secrets to your country’s enemies. In some countries, the punishment for treason can be life in prison. In some countries, the punishment for treason can be life in prison.

Slide.Title: treat (verb)
Slide.SlideText: treat (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to deal with; to act toward in a special way; 2) to try to cure Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) handle; regard; 2) care for Examples: Examples: He treats his employees generously. (handle) The therapist is treating the patient for a back injury. (care for) The therapist is treating the patient for a back injury.

Slide.Title: treatment (noun)
Slide.SlideText: treatment (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) the act of treating; 2) the use of medicine to try to cure or make better Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) handling; 2) cure, medication, regimen Examples: Examples: This package requires special treatment. (handling) What’s a good treatment for insomnia? (cure) Medicine is a treatment for illness. (cure) Medicine is a treatment for illness.

Slide.Title: treaty (noun)
Slide.SlideText: treaty (noun) Definition: Definition: a written agreement between two or more nations Synonyms: Synonyms: accord, covenant, pact Examples: Examples: Many countries have signed a treaty to eliminate nuclear weapons. When two countries end a war, they sign a peace treaty. When two countries end a war, they sign a peace treaty.

Slide.Title: trial (noun)
Slide.SlideText: trial (noun) Definition: Definition: a process for examining a question or dispute in a court of law to decide if a charge is true Synonyms: Synonyms: case, hearing, prosecution Examples: Examples: The accused thief is on trial now. Many newspaper reporters attended the trial. The witness did not seem nervous when he spoke at the trial. The witness did not seem nervous when he spoke at the trial.

Slide.Title: trick (verb)
Slide.SlideText: trick (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to cheat; 2) to fool people for the purpose of entertainment, or to get something Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) deceive, fool, outwit; 2) delude Examples: Examples: The investment firm tricked customers into buying worthless stock. (cheated) Magicians trick their audience into believing they have special powers. (delude) Magicians trick their audience into believing they have special powers.

Slide.Title: trip (noun)
Slide.SlideText: trip (noun) Definition: Definition: a movement from one place to another, usually a long distance Synonyms: Synonyms: journey, excursion, voyage Examples: Examples: He is away on a business trip. We are planning a trip to New York. Our biking trip in the French Alps lasted two weeks. Our biking trip in the French Alps lasted two weeks.

Slide.Title: trouble (noun)
Slide.SlideText: trouble (noun) Definition: Definition: that which causes concern, fear, difficulty, or problems Synonyms: Synonyms: disorder, disturbance, problem Examples: Examples: The company is in financial trouble. I do not want to cause you any trouble. My little brother likes to make trouble at school. My little brother likes to make trouble at school.

Slide.Title: truck (noun)
Slide.SlideText: truck (noun) Definition: Definition: a heavy vehicle used to carry goods Synonyms: Synonyms: pickup, rig, semi Examples: Examples: The street was blocked by a huge truck. He drives a truck for a living. We rented a truck to move our furniture. We rented a truck to move our furniture.

Slide.Title: tube (noun)
Slide.SlideText: tube (noun) Definition: Definition: a long, round structure through which solids, liquids, or gases can flow; or in which they can be kept Synonyms: Synonyms: cylinder, duct, pipette Examples: Examples: The subway in London is known as “the Tube.” Please buy a tube of toothpaste. An artist uses many tubes of paint to make a large painting. An artist uses many tubes of paint to make a large painting.

Slide.Title: turn (verb)
Slide.SlideText: turn (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to change direction; to move into a different position; 2) to change color, form, or shape Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) move, twist; 2) become, change, transform Examples: Examples: Please turn around and look at me. (move) I tossed and turned in bed all night. (twist) One day this caterpillar will turn into a beautiful butterfly. (change) One day this caterpillar will turn into a beautiful butterfly.
